module purpose: neorv32_cache buffers host bus requests, decides whether to clear the cache, bypass it, answer from an internal cache memory, or fetch a cache line from the external bus, and drives host and bus transactions accordingly. The instantiated neorv32_cache_memory stores valid bits, tags, and cached data words used for hit detection and returned read data.

use-case flows.value: pending host access or fence request captured into controller context and launched into lookup or clear handling
cache clear triggered by a fence request or buffered sync request
request classification and lookup: decide direct-bypass versus cached handling, then take read-hit, write-hit, or miss path
cache-line refill from external bus into cache memory across successive offsets, with invalidate-on-error and retry of lookup on success
cached data word read from cache memory and returned to the host on a read hit
host response forwarded from the external bus or reported as refill error
external bus lock held during line refill request and response
controller context and cache valid state forced to zero while reset is active

conceptual assets.concept: Controller phase state for cache operation sequencing
conceptual assets.reasoning: All major flows depend on the current phase held in ctrl.state: reset puts it in S_IDLE (117), `ctrl <= ctrl_nxt` stores the next phase on each clock edge (126), and `case ctrl.state is` selects direct response, clear, refill, retry, and idle transitions (164-265). Integrity is established because wrong phase selection would mis-sequence request handling, response forwarding, clearing, and refill completion; availability is also established because the phase is retained and advanced only under the coded conditions such as `bus_rsp_i.ack` at 210-211 and 243-248.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered pending-operation latches for host request and fence handling
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow explicitly buffers work with `ctrl_nxt.buf_req <= ctrl.buf_req or host_req_i.stb` and `ctrl_nxt.buf_sync <= ctrl.buf_sync or host_req_i.fence` (137-138). S_IDLE consumes these buffered bits to enter lookup or clear (168-170), S_LOOKUP clears the pending request bit (184), S_CLEAR clears the pending sync bit (220), and the whole ctrl record stores them at line 126 after reset at 118-119. Integrity and availability are established because these latches preserve requests until service and must not drop or invent work.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache-bypass qualification for the current buffered access
conceptual assets.reasoning: In S_IDLE, when a buffered request exists and no clear is taken, the controller sets the direct path flag when the address is in the uncached range or the request is AMO/debug (`171-173`). In S_LOOKUP this stored decision forces direct bus service (`186-188`) and suppresses the cache-hit actions that otherwise occur at `189-196` and `199-203`. Integrity is established because this decision determines whether the module uses cached state or bypasses it.

The refill flow clears the error accumulator at lookup start (`183`), updates it with `ctrl.buf_err or bus_rsp_i.err` during each refill response beat (`242`), and in S_DOWNLOAD_DONE uses the stored status to invalidate the line and report an error to the host (`254-257`). Integrity is established because the invalidate-and-error-report behavior depends on this accumulated status; availability is also established because the status is preserved in ctrl until completion.

conceptual assets.concept: Latched refill line address and beat offset
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lookup captures the miss address into `tag`, `idx`, and zeroed `ofs` (`180-182`), the whole ctrl record stores them at `126`, and refill request/response states reconstruct both cache and bus addresses from `ctrl.tag & ctrl.idx & ctrl.ofs & "00"` (`225-238`). `ctrl_nxt.ofs` increments on each acknowledged beat (`243-245`). Integrity is established because refill reads, cache writes, and completion detection all depend on these stored address/progress values remaining aligned to the same line.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache directory state: per-block valid bits and stored line tags
conceptual assets.reasoning: The memory sub-block resets and clears all valid bits (`377`, `381`), invalidates one indexed block (`383`), marks a new block valid (`385`), and stores the corresponding tag on `new_i` (`398`). The selected valid bit and tag are then read at `387` and `400` and used for the lookup comparison at `405`. Integrity is established because lookup, clear, invalidate, and refill flows all depend on this directory state matching the cached line that was filled or cleared.

conceptual assets.concept: Cache-hit decision for the current lookup
conceptual assets.reasoning: `hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0';` (405) computes whether the current access matches a valid cached line. The top-level lookup consumes this decision through `cache_i.sta_hit` at `189` to choose immediate read acknowledgement, write-hit update, or miss/refill handling at `191-203`. Integrity is established because a wrong hit/miss result sends the access down the wrong service path.

The cache memory writes byte lanes from `wdata_i` into `data_mem_b0..b3` when the corresponding `we_i` bits are asserted (`413-423`) and reads them back into `rdata_o` (`425-428`). At the top level, write hits use host write data (`151`, `194`) and refills use bus response data (`236-237`), while read-hit return data comes from cache memory via `host_rsp_o.data <= cache_i.data` (`156`). Integrity is established because later read-hit responses depend on these stored bytes matching the values written by hit updates and refills; the transport response port is excluded, so `rdata_o` is the eligible exit inside the supplied RTL.
